name: Tadalafil BPH dose-finding trial
question: Does once-daily tadalafil improve lower urinary tract symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia compared with placebo?

design.population: 1,058 men with lower urinary tract symptoms associated with clinical benign prostatic hyperplasia.
design.locator: Roehrborn 2008 PubMed abstract, Methods; NCT00384930 Study Design and Participant Flow

verdictNote: All doses improved IPSS; 5 mg had the authors' preferred risk-benefit profile.
takeaway: After 12 weeks, once-daily tadalafil 2.5, 5, 10, or 20 mg improved International Prostate Symptom Scores versus placebo in men with BPH-associated lower urinary tract symptoms; the authors favored 5 mg for its risk-benefit profile.

reports.label: Dose-finding trial
reports.citation: Roehrborn CG, McVary KT, Elion-Mboussa A, et al. "Tadalafil Administered Once Daily for Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Secondary to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: A Dose Finding Study." *J Urol.* 2008;180(4):1228-1234. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2008.06.079

results.measure: Least-squares mean IPSS change at endpoint, 2.5 mg versus placebo
Least-squares mean IPSS change at endpoint, 5 mg versus placebo
Least-squares mean IPSS change at endpoint, 10 mg versus placebo
Least-squares mean IPSS change at endpoint, 20 mg versus placebo

results.note: No tadalafil dose significantly improved peak flow versus placebo.

harms.label: Treatment-emergent adverse events
harms.note: Reported as infrequent across tadalafil groups; dose-specific event rates were not given in the abstract.

delivery.label: Run-in and treatment
delivery.value: Four-week placebo run-in, then once-daily assigned treatment for 12 weeks.

reports.label: Erectile-function subgroup
reports.citation: Porst H, McVary KT, Montorsi F, et al. "Effects of Once-Daily Tadalafil on Erectile Function in Men with Erectile Dysfunction and Signs and Symptoms of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia." *Eur Urol.* 2009;56(4):727-735. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2009.04.033

results.measure: Least-squares mean erectile-function domain change, 5 mg versus placebo
results.note: Post hoc analysis among 581 sexually active men with erectile dysfunction and BPH-associated LUTS.

reports.label: Uroflowmetry analysis
reports.citation: Roehrborn CG, Kaminetsky JC, Auerbach SM, et al. "Changes in Peak Urinary Flow and Voiding Efficiency in Men with Signs and Symptoms of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia during Once Daily Tadalafil Treatment." *BJU Int.* 2010;105(4):502-507. doi:10.1111/j.1464-410X.2009.08822.x

results.measure: Percentage increase in peak urinary flow, 5 mg versus placebo
results.note: Post hoc between-group comparison did not reach statistical significance; postvoid residual did not change significantly.

reports.label: One-year open-label extension
reports.citation: Donatucci CF, Brock GB, Goldfischer ER, et al. "Tadalafil Administered Once Daily for Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Secondary to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: A 1-Year, Open-Label Extension Study." *BJU Int.* 2011;107(7):1110-1116. doi:10.1111/j.1464-410X.2010.09687.x
reports.followUp: One-year open-label extension after 12-week randomized treatment

results.measure: Total IPSS change during one-year extension
results.note: The abstract reports that the symptom-score improvement was maintained, without a numerical change estimate.

harms.label: Treatment-emergent adverse events
harms.note: All extension participants received tadalafil 5 mg; no concurrent placebo group.

harms.label: Adverse-event discontinuation
harms.note: All extension participants received tadalafil 5 mg; no concurrent placebo group.

delivery.label: Extension participation and completion
delivery.value: 427 prior trial completers enrolled; 299/427 completed the one-year extension.
delivery.locator: Publisher abstract, Patients and Methods and Results
